title: Diagnose Windows fingerprint stability refusals with precise metadata and byte-count evidence
outcome: Explain and repair the confirmed cause of Windows B's two pre-stage fingerprint refusals without weakening source-change detection; first add precise bounded refusal diagnostics if original evidence cannot resolve the cause.
acceptance: Original Windows B failure artifacts and controlled probe results are preserved with locators and hashes; the outcome distinguishes observed facts from hypotheses and records the demonstrated failure cause or explicitly unresolved limits.

Fingerprint refusal diagnostics identify the failing phase and relevant metadata differences or expected/actual byte counts without removing any existing source-change detection checks, and targeted regressions verify the diagnostics and retained mutation rejection.
An independent cross-vendor review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher findings and the maintained full gate passes on the exact final input.
